map_ratio_picture.name: Ratios from a Picture (option)
map_ratio_picture.teaches: Write the ratio of two kinds of object shown in a picture (part:part and part:whole), then an equivalent ratio from grouped pictures
map_ratio_picture.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; two kinds of outline objects in a row; pupil writes the ratio in "___ : ___" slots, then one equivalent ratio. Screen: number boxes (production, never MC)
map_ratio_picture.why: ratio_intro and equiv_ratios are text-only; MAP shows a picture of objects and asks for the ratio
problemTypes: part:part — a row of 3 stars and 5 circles — write stars : circles / number boxes
part:whole — same picture — write stars : all objects / number boxes
equivalent — picture doubled (two rows) — write the new ratio and the simplest one / number boxes
levels: L1: part:part, objects grouped by kind; the two kinds labelled under the slots (label = hint, fades)
L2: part:part, objects mixed in the row; labels stay as words only
L3: part:whole from the same pictures; ratio frame "___ : ___" is structural and stays
L4: write an equivalent ratio from a repeated picture; no labels

example.item: There are 2 squares and 6 triangles. Write the ratio of squares to triangles.

misconceptions: writes the ratio in the wrong order (triangles : squares)
gives part:whole when part:part is asked
adds instead of scaling for the equivalent ratio

map_share_among.name: Share Among M, and Make Groups by Dragging (option)
map_share_among.teaches: Partitive division (deal N counters into M circles, how many in each) beside the existing quotitive form, with an on-screen drag response for both modes
map_share_among.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; N outline counters above M empty circles (share) or loose counters with ring outlines (group); pupil draws the counters in, writes "___ in each" / "___ groups" and the ÷ equation. Screen: drag counters into circles that snap, then type the number (production, not MC)

map.taskType: drag objects into groups; number entry

map_share_among.why: share_into_groups deals only "make groups of k" with count-only entry; MAP asks "share equally, how many each" and lets pupils drag. Lead ruling: one option, not two.
problemTypes: share — 12 counters, 3 circles — draw/drag them in, write ___ in each / drag + number box
group — 12 counters, "make groups of 4" — ring them, write ___ groups / drag + number box
equation — after sharing — write 12 ÷ 3 = ___ / number boxes
levels: L1: share among 2 with the circles drawn and one counter already placed in each (hint, fades)
L2: share among 2-5, circles drawn, no counter placed
L3: group mode (groups of k) beside share mode, one mode per page
L4: write the ÷ equation after sharing; the circles stay (structural)

example.item: Share 15 apples equally between 3 baskets. How many in each basket?

misconceptions: deals unequally (first circle gets the extras)
answers the number of groups instead of the number in each

map_array_to_eq.name: Picture to Multiplication Equation (option)
map_array_to_eq.teaches: Look at an array or equal groups and write the full equation ___ × ___ = ___ (and the reverse: given an equation, choose/draw the matching array)
map_array_to_eq.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; a dot array or ringed equal groups; pupil writes ___ × ___ = ___ (and ___ + ___ + ___ = ___ for repeated addition). Reverse: equation given, pupil rings rows on a dot grid. Screen: three number boxes; reverse = click rows/columns to shade (production)
map_array_to_eq.why: arrays_groups uses a sentence frame "rows of make in all"; MAP shows a picture and asks which/what equation, and the reverse direction is not dealt
problemTypes: picture → equation — 3 rows of 4 dots — write 3 × 4 = 12 / number boxes
groups → repeated addition and × — 4 rings of 2 — write 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 and 4 × 2 = 8 / number boxes
equation → picture — 2 × 5 given — shade 2 rows of 5 on a dot grid / click to shade
levels: L1: picture → equation with the frame "___ rows of ___" printed above the slots (hint, fades)
L2: picture → equation, × frame only (structural)
L3: groups → repeated addition and × equation together
L4: equation → picture (reverse)

example.item: An array has 4 rows with 6 dots in each row. Write the multiplication equation.

misconceptions: counts dots on the edge only
in the reverse, shades 6 rows of 4 and thinks it is wrong (does not see commutativity)

map_frac_model_match.name: Match Fraction Models and Numbers (option)
map_frac_model_match.teaches: Match each fraction model (area, bar, set) to its fraction from a bank, both directions
map_frac_model_match.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; 3-4 fraction models (area, bar, set) on the left, a bank of fractions on the right; pupil writes the letter of the model beside each fraction. Screen: drag each fraction to its model (production pairing, not single MC)
map_frac_model_match.why: identify deals one model at a time (write or MC); MAP match-the-two form missing
problemTypes: model → fraction — 4 shaded models, bank of 4 fractions — write/drag the match
fraction → model — 4 fractions, 4 models with one distractor — write the letter / drag
mixed kinds — one area, one bar, one set model — match each
levels: L1: area models only, unit fractions, bank of 3
L2: non-unit fractions, bank of 4
L3: mixed model kinds (area, bar, set)
L4: one distractor model with unequal parts (the equal-parts rule)

example.item: Match each picture to its fraction: A (2 of 3 parts shaded), B (1 of 4 parts shaded). Bank: 1/4, 2/3.

misconceptions: counts shaded over unshaded instead of over all parts

map_decimal_grid.name: Decimal Grids and Numbers
map_decimal_grid.teaches: Read a tenths strip or hundred square as a decimal and fraction, shade a grid for a given decimal, and match grids to decimals
map_decimal_grid.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; a tenths strip or hundred square in a boxed cell; pupil writes the decimal and the fraction, or shades the grid for a given decimal. Screen: number boxes; shade by clicking squares (production)
map_decimal_grid.why: No decimal skill reads or shades a decimal grid (percent_visual does percent only)
problemTypes: grid → decimal — 37 of 100 squares shaded — write 0.37 and 37/100 / number boxes
decimal → grid — 0.6 given — shade the strip / click to shade
match — 3 grids, 3 decimals — pair them / drag
levels: L1: tenths strip, write the decimal; place-value header "ones . tenths" printed (structural, stays)
L2: hundred square, whole rows + loose squares
L3: shade for a given decimal
L4: match 3 grids to 3 decimals including 0.4 vs 0.04

example.item: A hundred square has 52 squares shaded. Write the shaded part as a decimal.

map_nl_read_decimal.name: Read a Decimal on a Number Line (option)
map_nl_read_decimal.teaches: Name the decimal at a marked point on a tenths/hundredths line (the reverse of placing)
map_nl_read_decimal.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; a tenths or hundredths number line with an arrow at one tick; pupil writes the decimal in a box. Screen: number box (production, never MC)
map_nl_read_decimal.why: decimal_nl_drag only places; fractions have both directions, decimals do not
problemTypes: read tenths — 0 to 1 by tenths, arrow at 7th tick — write 0.7
read hundredths — 2.3 to 2.4 by hundredths — write 2.36
read on a line labelled only at ends — find the step first, then write
levels: L1: tenths, every tick labelled except the arrowed one (labels = hint, fade)
L2: tenths, ends labelled only
L3: hundredths between two tenths
L4: line starting at a non-zero whole (2.3 to 2.4)

example.item: A number line goes from 4 to 5 in tenths. The arrow is on the third tick after 4. What number is it?

map_frac_unit_build.name: Build a Fraction from Unit Fractions (option)
map_frac_unit_build.teaches: Count unit fractions: 3/4 is 3 parts of size 1/4; write the fraction as a sum of unit fractions from a picture
map_frac_unit_build.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; a bar or area model cut into equal parts with some shaded; pupil writes the unit-fraction sum and the total (1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 3/4). Reverse: sum given, pupil shades. Screen: number boxes for the sum; click to shade for the reverse (production)
map_frac_unit_build.why: decompose_fractions covers 4th grade; unit-fraction counting at grade 3 MAP band not dealt from a picture
problemTypes: model → sum — 3 of 4 parts shaded — write 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 3/4
sum → model — 1/5 + 1/5 given — shade the bar / click to shade
model → count — "how many fifths?" — write 3 fifths = 3/5
levels: L1: count the shaded unit parts, "___ quarters" frame (hint, fades)
L2: write the unit-fraction sum, frame slots for each addend (structural)
L3: reverse: shade from the sum
L4: sums past 1 (5/4 = 1/4 × 5) with two bars

example.item: A bar is cut into 6 equal parts and 4 are shaded. Write the shaded part as a sum of unit fractions.

misconceptions: writes the number of shaded parts as the denominator

map_power10_exponent.name: Powers of Ten: Patterns and Exponents
map_power10_exponent.teaches: Multiply and divide whole numbers and decimals by 10, 100, 1000 and 10^n; explain the zeros/point shift; write 10^3 = 1000
map_power10_exponent.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; a place-value chart under the calculation with arrows showing the shift; pupil writes the product/quotient and, at L4, the exponent form. Screen: number boxes (production)
map_power10_exponent.why: mult_zeros is whole-number only; dec_missing (placevalue:place_value_10x) is missing-number only; exponent notation not dealt
problemTypes: exponent — 10³ — write 1,000 and 7 × 10³ = 7,000
levels: L1: whole × / ÷ 10, 100, 1000 with the pv chart (live skill level)
L2: decimal × 10, 100, 1000; pv chart stays (structural), arrow hint fades
L3: decimal ÷ 10, 100
L4: powers of ten written as 10^n
misconceptions: moves the point the wrong way

map_frac_compare_reason.name: Compare Fractions Using 1/2 (option)
map_frac_compare_reason.teaches: Compare two fractions by placing each against 1/2 or 1 (no common denominator)
map_frac_compare_reason.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; two fractions with a 0-1/2-1 strip beneath each; pupil writes >, <, = and ticks "more than half / less than half" for each. Screen: sign box + click the benchmark side (production)
map_frac_compare_reason.why: compare uses models of same whole only; benchmark reasoning is a MAP 201-210 task
problemTypes: compare to 1/2 — 3/8 and 4/6 — tick each side of 1/2, write the sign
compare to 1 — 7/8 and 5/4 — tick each side of 1
justify — choose the reason from a bank ("3/8 is less than half because 3 < 4")
levels: L1: one fraction at a time against 1/2 with the strip (strip = hint, fades)
L2: two fractions, strip shown
L3: two fractions, no strip, write the sign
L4: benchmark 1 and reason from a bank

map_percent_of_grid_bar.name: Percent of a Number with a Bar (option)
map_percent_of_grid_bar.teaches: Find 10%, 25%, 50% of a number from a percent bar model
map_percent_of_grid_bar.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; a percent bar 0-100% above a number bar 0-N; pupil writes the value at 10%, 25%, 50%. Screen: number boxes (production)
problemTypes: 10% — bar of 70 — write 7, then 30% = 21
percent of grid — hundred square with 30 shaded, whole = 200 — write 60
levels: L1: 50% with the bar halved (hint mark, fades)
L3: 10% then multiples of 10%
L4: no bar, number only (live skill level)
misconceptions: divides by 25 instead of finding a quarter

decimal_pv.name: Tenths and Hundredths in a Place-Value Chart
decimal_pv.teaches: Decimal place value: value of a digit in tenths/hundredths
decimal_pv.representation: B&W place-value chart cell; number entry on screen

map.taskType: value of the digit, number entry

decimal_pv.why: MAP asks the value of a decimal digit; no decimal place-value skill exists
decimal_pv.mapClause: value of a digit to thousandths: the 7 in 3.072 is 7 hundredths (0.07); chart extends to thousandths

div_frac_frac.name: Divide Fractions by Fractions
div_frac_frac.representation: B&W bar model cell; fraction entry
div_frac_frac.why: Top MAP 3-5 band reaches 6th-grade fraction division

comparison_statements.name: Times as Many: Statements and Equations (option)
comparison_statements.why: MAP asks which equation matches "35 is 5 times as many as 7"

dec_compare_model.name: Compare Decimals With Models (option)
dec_compare_model.representation: B&W hundred-square beside each decimal; symbol entry

decimal_models.name: Decimal Operations With Models (option)
decimal_models.representation: B&W hundred squares beside the column
decimal_models.why: MAP shows decimal models for adding

ratio_problems.name: Ratio and Proportion Problems
ratio_problems.teaches: Ratio word problems with bar models

mult_mixed_int.name: Multiply a Mixed Number by an Integer (option)

frac_beyond_1.name: Fractions Beyond 1
frac_beyond_1.why: models of several wholes not dealt

mult_dec_dec.name: Multiply Decimals by Decimals (option)
mult_dec_dec.teaches: decimal × decimal with the standard algorithm

share_group.name: Share and Make Groups
share_group.representation: B&W boxed cell per WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD; production answer on screen (number entry / drag), not MC
share_group.why: No early share/group skill; WRM share_group reused.

long_mult.name: Long Multiplication and Division (4-digit)
long_mult.representation: B&W boxed cell per WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD; production answer on screen (number entry / drag), not MC
long_mult.why: 4-digit × 2-digit long multiplication not dealt; WRM long_mult reused.

mult_three.name: Multiply Three Numbers
mult_three.representation: B&W boxed cell per WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD; production answer on screen (number entry / drag), not MC
mult_three.why: No three-factor skill; WRM proposal reused.
mult_three.mapClause: associative property with brackets: (2 × 3) × 4 = 2 × (3 × 4), fill the missing factor

map_div_tens.name: Divide by Multiples of Ten (option)
map_div_tens.teaches: Dividing by 10s using the basic fact (360 ÷ 40 = 36 ÷ 4), quotient a whole number
map_div_tens.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; the basic fact printed above in grey support row (36 ÷ 4 = 9), then the target 360 ÷ 40 = ___ ; pupil writes the quotient. Screen: number box (production)
map_div_tens.why: divide deals facts only; MAP places dividing by a multiple of 10 at 201-210
problemTypes: divide by tens — 360 ÷ 40 — write 9 (fact 36 ÷ 4)
tens ÷ ones — 360 ÷ 4 — write 90
find the fact — 2,400 ÷ 60 — write the fact and 40
levels: L1: dividend ÷ one-digit with tens (360 ÷ 4), fact row printed (hint, fades)
L2: tens ÷ tens (360 ÷ 40), fact row printed
L3: no fact row
L4: hundreds ÷ tens (2,400 ÷ 60)

map_equal_frac_build.name: Fractions Equal to a Mixed Number (option)
map_equal_frac_build.teaches: Writing several fractions equal to a whole or mixed number (1 1/3 = 4/3 = 8/6) using a digit bank
map_equal_frac_build.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; a whole or mixed number with 2-3 empty fraction frames and a digit bank under it; pupil writes digits into the frames. Screen: drag digit tiles into the boxes (production)
map_equal_frac_build.why: whole_as_fraction writes only n/1 and d/d; MAP asks several equivalents of a mixed number with digit tiles
problemTypes: whole — 1 = ___/___ (3 frames) — fill from the bank
improper → mixed — 7/4 = ___ ___/4
levels: L1: equal to 1, denominators printed (hint, fades)
L2: equal to 2 or 3 wholes
L3: mixed number to improper, denominators printed
L4: chain of equivalents, no denominators printed
misconceptions: adds the whole to the numerator (2 1/2 = 3/2)
doubles only one part of the fraction

map_est_both_factors.option: factors: "both multi-digit" (3-/4-digit × 2-digit, round both factors), beside the existing place and task (compute / closest / reasonable) options
map_est_both_factors.name: Estimate Products: Round Both Factors (option)
map_est_both_factors.teaches: Round both factors of a 3- or 4-digit × 2-digit product to estimate it and judge whether an answer is reasonable
map_est_both_factors.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; "412 × 38 ≈ ___ × ___ = ___" slots with the rounded factors written first. Screen: the same inline number boxes; the reasonable task is a yes/no tick plus the estimate (production)
map_est_both_factors.why: estimate_products rounds only the bigger factor of 2-4-digit × 1-digit; MAP 211-220 estimates multi-digit × multi-digit. Option on the live skill, not a new skill.
problemTypes: round both — 412 × 38 — write 400 × 40 = 16,000
reasonable? — "Sam says 297 × 21 = 2,237" — write the estimate, tick yes/no
closest — choose the estimate nearest to 58 × 69 (live task, larger factors)
levels: L1: 2-digit × 2-digit, round both to tens; "round to" labels printed (hint, fades)
L2: 3-digit × 2-digit, round to hundreds and tens
L3: 4-digit × 2-digit
L4: "is the answer reasonable?" with the estimate

map_mult_prop_grouping.option: response: "choose ALL equal products" (order, breaking apart, ×1/×0 expressions mixed with distractors)
map_mult_prop_grouping.name: Multiplication Properties: Choose All Equal (option)
map_mult_prop_grouping.teaches: Recognise every expression equal to a given product using the properties the skill already teaches (order, breaking apart, ×1, ×0). Three-factor grouping is NOT here: reused mult_three owns it.
map_mult_prop_grouping.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; a target product and 4-5 expressions, pupil ticks every equal one. Screen: click ALL (multi-select-check), production of the set
map_mult_prop_grouping.why: mult_properties asks for one missing number; MAP asks which expressions are equal. Associative/three factors is owned by mult_three (row "Multiply three numbers").
problemTypes: order — "Tick every expression equal to 6 × 8" (8 × 6, 6 + 8, 6 × 9) — tick / click all
breaking apart — "equal to 7 × 6" (7 × 5 + 7 × 1, 7 × 3 + 7 × 3, 7 + 6) — tick
levels: L1: one property per item, 3 expressions, property named above (hint, fades)
L2: one property, 4 expressions, no name
L3: two properties mixed
L4: 5 expressions with an addition distractor (6 + 8)
misconceptions: splits both factors in breaking apart (4 × 7 = 2 × 5 + 2 × 2)

map_nl_hops_equation.option: task: "write the equation the hops show" (hops drawn, no equation printed)
map_nl_hops_equation.name: Number Line Hops to Equation (option)
map_nl_hops_equation.teaches: Read equal hops on a number line and write ___ × ___ = ___
map_nl_hops_equation.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; the hop line with equal hops drawn and no equation; pupil writes ___ × ___ = ___. Screen: three number boxes (never MC)
map_nl_hops_equation.why: nl_mult always prints the equation and asks the product; MAP shows the hops and asks the equation.
problemTypes: hops → × — 4 hops of 5 from 0 — write 4 × 5 = 20
hops → repeated addition — write 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20
which hops — two lines drawn, write the letter of the one showing 3 × 6 and its product
levels: L1: every hop end labelled (hint, fades)
L2: only 0 and the end labelled
L3: the repeated addition and the × equation
L4: pick the matching line of two

example.item: The number line shows 6 hops of 3 from 0. Write the multiplication equation.

misconceptions: counts tick marks instead of hops
writes hop size first and number of hops second and thinks order matters
reads the end point as the number of hops

equal_groups_early.name: Make Equal Groups
equal_groups_early.teaches: recognising, making and adding equal groups, and doubles as two equal groups; MAP clause: move objects so two groups are equal
equal_groups_early.representation: groups drawn in rings; tick equal or not, write groups of and the repeated addition. Print: B&W boxed cell, outline cubes in two rings, pupil draws/crosses out to make them equal and writes the count. Screen: drag cubes between rings (snap), then type the count; never MC

map.taskType: drag objects to make groups equal

equal_groups_early.why: No live skill moves objects to equalise groups; WRM equal_groups_early reused.

map_decimal_expanded.option: band: "decimals" (tenths, hundredths, thousandths) + direction (to expanded / to standard)
map_decimal_expanded.name: Expanded Form with Decimals (option)
map_decimal_expanded.teaches: Write a decimal to thousandths in expanded form with fractions or decimals, and the reverse (5.NBT.A.3a)
map_decimal_expanded.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; a place-value chart header (ones . tenths hundredths thousandths) in grey, slots "___ + ___ × 1/10 + ___ × 1/100"; pupil writes digits. Screen: number boxes in the frame (production, never MC)
map_decimal_expanded.why: expand stops at whole numbers; MAP 211-220 asks decimal expanded form.
problemTypes: to expanded (decimal form) — 3.47 — write 3 + 0.4 + 0.07 / number boxes
to expanded (fraction form) — 3.47 — write 3 + 4 × 1/10 + 7 × 1/100
to standard — 5 + 0.2 + 0.006 — write 5.206 / number box
levels: L1: tenths only, chart header with digits under it (hint row, fades)
L2: hundredths, decimal form (0.4 + 0.07); chart header stays (structural)
L3: fraction form (4 × 1/10)
L4: thousandths with a zero digit; reverse direction
misconceptions: drops the zero place in the reverse (5 + 0.2 + 0.006 = 5.26)

map_decimal_word_form.option: band: "decimals" (tenths, hundredths, thousandths), with the existing wordform direction (to_number / to_words)
map_decimal_word_form.name: Decimal Word Form (option)
map_decimal_word_form.teaches: Read and write decimals in words using the last place ("four and twenty-six hundredths") (5.NBT.A.3a)
map_decimal_word_form.representation: Print: one boxed B&W Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; the words on one line, numeral slots with a fixed decimal point below (or the numeral and a word bank to build the words). Screen: number entry for to_number; word tiles (drag) for to_words — production, never MC

map.taskType: number entry; build from word tiles

map_decimal_word_form.why: number_word_form deals whole numbers only; MAP 211-220 asks decimals in words and numerals.
problemTypes: words → numeral — "seven and three tenths" — write 7.3
words → numeral with a zero — "two and five hundredths" — write 2.05
numeral → words — 4.26 — build "four and twenty-six hundredths" from tiles
levels: L1: tenths, the decimal point slot printed (structural)
L2: hundredths without a zero
L3: hundredths/thousandths with a zero place
L4: numeral → words from a tile bank

example.item: Write as a number: nine and fourteen hundredths.

misconceptions: writes 2.5 for two and five hundredths
names the place of the first digit (4.26 = "twenty-six tenths")
